transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because people keep treating this foreclosure like it’s just paperwork or missed payments, but that’s not what’s happening. I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even some people at my job have been working together quietly to push me out of my house. They keep showing me papers like that’s supposed to settle it, but it doesn’t change what I’ve been seeing for almost two years.

Over the past two years, have you also noticed times when your mood, energy, or sleep changed dramatically—like feeling extremely low and hopeless, or unusually high, energetic, and needing little sleep—separate from your concerns about the house?

I don’t think so. I mean, it’s hard to separate anything from what’s going on with the house because that’s been hanging over me the whole time. But I haven’t noticed, like, big dramatic mood or energy swings on their own.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people around you didn't seem to notice or hear?
No, not really. I mean, I hear normal things like anyone else, but I’m not hearing voices or seeing things that other people can’t see. That’s not what this is.
Do you have any medical conditions, past head injuries, or use of drugs or alcohol that started or changed around the same time these beliefs about the house began?

I don’t think anything like that changed around then. I mean, I’m not aware of a head injury or some medical thing starting at the same time. And drugs or alcohol haven’t been part of this, at least not in any way I can connect to what’s happening with the house.
Have you noticed any recent problems with your memory, concentration, or confusion in your daily life?

I haven’t really noticed anything major like confusion. My memory seems about the same. Concentration can be hard sometimes, but I think that’s more because I’m stressed and preoccupied. I’m still managing my day-to-day stuff.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion (belief that bank, loan servicer, and coworkers are colluding to force her out of her home) persisting for nearly two years. There is no evidence of hallucinations, disorganized speech/behavior, or other psychotic features that would suggest schizophrenia. Mood symptoms consistent with mania or depression are explicitly denied, ruling out a mood disorder with psychotic features. No cognitive impairment, substance use, or medical/neurological condition temporally associated with symptom onset was identified, excluding a psychotic disorder due to another medical condition or substance. Functioning outside the delusional system appears largely preserved, consistent with delusional disorder rather than schizophrenia, where functioning is more broadly impaired.
